**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/23 (Tue) 23:17  
[USER] The user is trying to organize their movie watching history.  
[USER] The user has had some crazy movie binges lately, including watching all 22 Marvel Cinematic Universe movies in two weeks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant offered to help create a list to organize the user's movie watching history.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested three options for organizing the movie list:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] **Option 1: Simple Text List** - Use a note-taking app like Evernote, OneNote, or Google Docs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] **Option 2: Spreadsheet** - Create a table with columns for Movie Title, Release Year, Watch Date, Rating, Notes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] **Option 3: Movie Tracking Apps** - Suggested apps include Letterboxd, IMDb Watchlist, FilmAffinity, and Cinema Clock.  
[USER] The user prefers the spreadsheet option and requested help setting up the columns.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided a suggested template for the movie tracking spreadsheet with the following columns:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Movie Title  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Release Year  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Watch Date  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Rating  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Notes  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Franchise/Series  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Genre  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Format  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Re-watch  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant also provided optional columns: Director, Cast, Runtime, Language.  
[USER] The user decided to add a column for the type of movie (e.g., sequel, remake, standalone) and a column for the platform watched (e.g., Amazon Prime, in theaters).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant updated the template to include the new columns:

[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Platform
